name: Kale Fakes a Fall to Meet Ashley
description: Kale sits on the front steps, checking his watch and yawning. He sees Ashley's station wagon approaching and quickly stands, fixing his hair before walking toward the mailbox. As the car turns into the driveway, he leans against the mailbox as if he has slipped, reaching inside to grab the mail. Ashley pulls up, glances over, and sees him struggling. She gets out of the car and walks over. Kale tries to push himself up but his feet slip again. Ashley offers help and pulls him upright. She opens the mailbox, takes out the mail, and hands it to him. He thanks her, calling the moment humiliating. She remarks that he lost what was left of his pride a while ago. He introduces himself as Kale. She tells him her name is Ashley. They exchange a few words about her move and his ankle bracelet before Bonnie calls Ashley from inside the house. Ashley mentions her mother’s polite but firm tone, and Kale says he recognizes it. She goes inside, smiling, and Kale watches her go.

name: Kale and Ashley's Front Yard Conversation

Ashley retrieves the mail and hands it to him, making a remark about his lost pride. Kale jokes that the police had the wrong guy, then asks how the move went. Ashley says it’s still ongoing, and Kale gestures to his ankle bracelet, explaining he’s a little spatially challenged. Ashley steps closer, looks at the bracelet, and teases him about having a Martha Stewart vibe. Kale laughs, adding he doesn’t get the 48-hour allowance for office visits or a reality show. He asks where she moved from. She says she’s a city girl, born and raised, now forcefully relocated. Kale responds with a joke about taking her to a kegger in his Hummer, then turns to leave. Ashley smiles and calls after him, but is interrupted by her mother calling from inside the house. She quietly mentions her mother’s polite but firm tone, and Kale says he knows the tone. She tells him her name is Ashley, and he replies that he noticed. She goes inside, and Kale stands alone in the yard, watching her go.
